text: (emphasis added)] (a) [3:312] Compare—Ins.C. § 533: In addition, Ins.C. § 533 prohibits insurers from indemnifying an insured for liability resulting from the insured's “wilful act.” [Ins.C. § 533; see ¶ 3:105 ff.] ➪ [3:312.1] PRACTICE POINTER: Even when the plaintiff alleges only intentional torts, the insured should argue that coverage is triggered where the alleged facts or proffered evidence would support a potentially covered claim sounding in negligence; e.g., a complaint asserting sexual molestation may include a related claim of negligent nonsexual activity. See discussion at ¶ 3:113.5 ff. [3:313] Reserved. (2) [3:314] Workers' compensation: CGL policies specifically exclude any obligation of the insured under workers' compensation, disability benefits or unemployment compensation laws. [See CG 00 01 12 07, Sec. I, Coverage A, ¶ 2.d.] (3) [3:315] Employers' liability: CGL policies also exclude “bodily injury” claims arising out of and in the course of employment or in performing duties related to the conduct of the insured's business.
